latin.title: Already Latin: preserve spelling; optional locale-aware ASCII folding
latin.orthographic_method: NFC normalization and identity; optional explicit character-to-string folding for an ASCII slug
latin.readable_method: Preserve the existing Latin spelling, including meaningful marks where the output contract permits
latin.nlp: No for romanization; pronunciation/IPA transcription would be a different task
latin.one_to_one: Identity for normalized Latin spelling; ASCII folding is often one-to-many or many-to-one
latin.implementation: Unicode normalization plus small locale-specific tables; no neural model
latin.limits: Do not replace normal Latin spelling with English phonetics. Diacritics, tone marks, apostrophes and case can distinguish words. A language can use additional scripts even when CLDR's default is Latin.

cyrillic.title: Cyrillic: language-specific letter-to-string maps plus finite context
cyrillic.orthographic_method: Select a named language/standard table; normalize combining signs, match multigraphs where applicable, preserve case and soft/hard signs according to that standard
cyrillic.readable_method: Use a language-specific practical romanization; add finite word-position/context rules. Lexical pronunciation belongs in an optional separate profile
cyrillic.nlp: No for standard spelling romanization; optional lexicon for pronunciation and conventional proper names
cyrillic.one_to_one: Frequently character-to-string, not strict one-to-one; some schemes need digraph/context rules
cyrillic.implementation: Compiled tables or finite-state transducer; language-specific ICU/CLDR rules where verified
cyrillic.limits: The same Cyrillic letter can have different outputs across languages. A standard orthographic transform cannot reconstruct omitted distinctions or stress. Latin-to-Cyrillic ambiguity is a separate problem.

greek.title: Greek: standard-aware contextual rules
greek.orthographic_method: Apply the selected ELOT/ISO or bibliographic spelling scheme, including combining accents and digraph rules
greek.readable_method: Finite context for practical Modern Greek romanization; distinguish ancient/polytonic input and conventional names
greek.nlp: No learned model for the standard baseline; optional name overrides
greek.implementation: Finite-state rules plus explicit Modern/Ancient policy
greek.limits: A transliteration standard and a full phonetic transcription are different contracts.

armenian.title: Armenian: orthographic tables with ligature and variety handling
armenian.orthographic_method: Normalize ligatures and combining forms, then apply a named Armenian romanization table
armenian.readable_method: Select Eastern/Western Armenian pronunciation policy explicitly; add finite contextual rules and conventional-name overrides
armenian.nlp: No for bibliographic spelling; pronunciation needs variety information and possibly a lexicon
armenian.one_to_one: Not uniformly: multigraphs/ligatures and scheme-dependent outputs
armenian.implementation: Table plus longest-match/context rules; separate variety option
armenian.limits: The generic language code does not identify Eastern versus Western pronunciation.

georgian.title: Georgian: small standard-specific mapping
georgian.orthographic_method: Normalize script/case forms and use the chosen Georgian-to-Latin table
georgian.readable_method: Use the selected practical scheme, preserving its ejective/distinction markers
georgian.one_to_one: Character-to-string mapping; some letters become multicharacter Latin sequences
georgian.implementation: Small tables and Unicode case/script normalization
georgian.limits: ASCII punctuation removal can destroy distinctions in the selected scheme.

arabic-missing-vowels.title: Arabic-derived scripts with missing vowels: separate spelling from pronunciation
arabic-missing-vowels.orthographic_method: Normalize presentation forms and combining marks conservatively; apply a language-specific spelling transliteration table without inventing omitted vowels
arabic-missing-vowels.readable_method: Tokenization, morphology/lexical readings and contextual vowel prediction, followed by deterministic romanization; use a compact specialist model when it improves held-out accuracy
arabic-missing-vowels.nlp: Yes for inferred-vowel readable output; no for source-faithful spelling conversion
arabic-missing-vowels.one_to_one: Possible only for a spelling representation; source text may not contain enough information for one unique spoken reading
arabic-missing-vowels.implementation: Rules plus language-specific lexicon/morphology and optional small contextual model; expose spelling and pronunciation modes separately
arabic-missing-vowels.limits: Dialect, names, loanwords and short inputs remain ambiguous. Arabic rules must not be reused unchanged for Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Sindhi or other languages.

arabic-vowels-written.title: Arabic-derived alphabets that explicitly encode most vowels
arabic-vowels-written.orthographic_method: Language-specific letter-to-string mapping with finite rules for vowel carriers, joins and combining marks
arabic-vowels-written.readable_method: Use the selected Latin orthography; add exceptions for loans and names if required
arabic-vowels-written.nlp: No learned model as the baseline; optional lexicon for exceptional readings
arabic-vowels-written.one_to_one: Mostly table-driven, with context/normalization rather than a universal Arabic mapping
arabic-vowels-written.implementation: Tables and a small finite-state rule layer
arabic-vowels-written.limits: This profile applies to the identified language and orthography, not to all Arabic-script text.

jawi.title: Malay Jawi: spelling conversion plus lexical vowel recovery
jawi.orthographic_method: Map Jawi-specific letters and preserve the vowels actually written
jawi.readable_method: Recover standard Rumi word spellings using a Malay lexicon and contextual disambiguation; train a small model only after assessing dictionary/rule baselines
jawi.nlp: Lexical/contextual processing for conventional Rumi output; no for a literal spelling representation
jawi.one_to_one: No for standard Malay word spellings because Jawi does not uniquely spell out every Rumi vowel
jawi.implementation: Jawi-specific normalization and mapping, lexicon, optional sequence model
jawi.limits: A generic Arabic romanizer will mishandle additional Jawi letters and missing-vowel choices.

hebrew.title: Hebrew: pointed spelling rules; lexical/contextual readings for unpointed text
hebrew.orthographic_method: Map consonants and written niqqud under a named scheme, with combining-mark normalization
hebrew.readable_method: Use word readings/morphology and a vowel-restoration model or lexicon for unpointed text; then render the chosen romanization standard
hebrew.nlp: Yes for reliable inferred pronunciation of unpointed words; no for consonantal spelling conversion
hebrew.one_to_one: No for readable output: vowels and some pronunciation distinctions may be absent
hebrew.implementation: Rules plus lexicon/context model; proper-name override support
hebrew.limits: A chosen name spelling can be conventional rather than mechanically recoverable.

yiddish.title: Yiddish: standard-specific digraph rules with limited lexical exceptions
yiddish.orthographic_method: Normalize pointing and longest-match Yiddish letter combinations under the selected standard
yiddish.readable_method: Apply the selected standard's Yiddish rules; use a dictionary/list for traditionally Hebrew-spelled forenames and other demonstrated exceptions
yiddish.nlp: No learned model for the standard rule-first baseline; narrow lexical exceptions may need a dictionary
yiddish.one_to_one: No: longest-match digraph/pointing rules and limited lexical exceptions
yiddish.implementation: Finite-state rules plus a curated name/exception layer
yiddish.limits: ALA-LC's standardized Yiddish table ignores etymology; do not require a lexicon for the whole Hebrew/Aramaic-derived component. Other pronunciation targets may choose different rules.

indic-lexical.title: Indic abugidas: deterministic spelling transliteration; language-specific reading rules
indic-lexical.orthographic_method: Parse orthographic syllables: consonants, dependent vowels, virama, conjuncts, nukta and nasal signs; render a named scheme
indic-lexical.readable_method: Apply the language's inherent-vowel/schwa behavior, syllable rules and lexical exceptions; morphology or a small G2P model where validated
indic-lexical.nlp: Language-specific rules and often lexicon/morphology for pronunciation; no learned model required for structural spelling transliteration
indic-lexical.one_to_one: No: consonant-vowel state, combining signs and conjuncts require an algorithm
indic-lexical.implementation: Shared script parser plus separate language phonology profiles; optional compact G2P
indic-lexical.limits: A Hindi schwa-deletion rule is not a universal Devanagari or Indic rule. Low-resource languages require native review and language-specific evidence before a pronunciation guarantee.

indic-structural.title: Indic abugidas with a rule-first romanization baseline
indic-structural.orthographic_method: Parse consonant-vowel sequences, virama/conjuncts, vowel marks and orthographic variants before Latin rendering
indic-structural.readable_method: Use language-specific contextual phonology; add a lexicon/model only for measured exceptions or pronunciation requirements
indic-structural.nlp: No learned model for conservative standard romanization; optional lexical processing for fuller pronunciation
indic-structural.one_to_one: No: syllable and combining-sign algorithms are needed
indic-structural.implementation: Script parser and finite-state language rules; optional name exceptions
indic-structural.limits: The script parser can be shared, but each language's reading rules and standard must be separate.

sanskrit.title: Sanskrit: structural conversion to IAST or another named scheme
sanskrit.orthographic_method: Parse Devanagari vowel/consonant state, virama, conjuncts and Vedic/combining signs; render IAST or a selected alternative
sanskrit.readable_method: Preserve the written Sanskrit forms under the chosen standard; splitting sandhi or recovering words is an optional separate analysis
sanskrit.nlp: No for standard written transliteration; sandhi segmentation is a different NLP feature
sanskrit.one_to_one: No code-point substitution: inherent vowels and combining signs require state
sanskrit.implementation: Indic structural transliterator with Sanskrit-specific conventions
sanskrit.limits: Keep diacritics for scholarly output; ASCII modes are alternate schemes, not reversible accent stripping.

ethiopic.title: Ethiopic: syllable tables with language-specific conventions
ethiopic.orthographic_method: Map the encoded syllabic series/order, punctuation and numerals using the language's standard
ethiopic.readable_method: Add sixth-order vowel/zero-vowel and other language-specific conventions; lexical information is needed if unmarked gemination/full pronunciation must be reconstructed
ethiopic.nlp: No learned model for standard spelling romanization; lexical/phonological layer for fuller pronunciation
ethiopic.one_to_one: Syllable-to-string table plus rules, not letter-to-letter
ethiopic.implementation: Compact syllabary map with separate Amharic/Tigrinya profiles
ethiopic.limits: Shared Ethiopic characters do not make Amharic and Tigrinya pronunciation identical.

mandarin.title: Mandarin option when selected: word readings and polyphone disambiguation
mandarin.orthographic_method: A character-reading fallback is possible but is not a reliable word pronunciation; choose the reading language explicitly
mandarin.readable_method: Mandarin phrase/word readings plus polyphone disambiguation and a deterministic Hanyu Pinyin renderer; optional tone and word-boundary policies
mandarin.nlp: Lexical/contextual reading selection; a small classifier is an appropriate candidate
mandarin.one_to_one: No: Han characters can have multiple readings, and word boundaries/readings require context
mandarin.implementation: Phrase lexicon plus compact polyphone model; deterministic Pinyin formatting
mandarin.limits: Use for zh-CN/zh-TW in this report is conditional on an explicitly selected Mandarin reading profile, not inferred solely from locale. Hans/Hant identifies writing form, not spoken language. Names/regional readings need overrides. Simplified/traditional conversion is separate.

cantonese.title: Cantonese Han text: Cantonese readings and a chosen standard
cantonese.orthographic_method: Select Cantonese lexical readings; generic Mandarin character data is unsuitable
cantonese.readable_method: Cantonese word/phrase lexicon and contextual pronunciation selection followed by a Jyutping or selected-standard renderer
cantonese.nlp: Lexical/contextual processing; specialist model optional after a lexicon baseline
cantonese.implementation: Cantonese-specific data and disambiguation, shared Han segmentation infrastructure where useful
cantonese.limits: Traditional Chinese characters do not imply Cantonese; explicit yue/romanization selection is required.

han-policy.title: Han language/reading policy must be selected
han-policy.orthographic_method: Preserve written text or require a reading-language/profile selection before pronunciation romanization
han-policy.readable_method: Route to Mandarin, Cantonese, another reading tradition, or a Literary Chinese profile according to an explicit contract
han-policy.nlp: Lexicon/context after selecting the reading language; language choice is not recoverable from script alone
han-policy.implementation: Explicit profile routing, language-specific lexicons and compact reading models
han-policy.limits: A locale such as Hong Kong or a Literary Chinese label does not uniquely determine the intended pronunciation system.

japanese.title: Japanese: morphological readings, then kana romanization
japanese.orthographic_method: Kana-to-Latin is algorithmic; arbitrary Kanji cannot be assigned reliable readings by a character table
japanese.readable_method: Morphological tokenizer with lexical readings, name handling and optional disambiguation; then render Hepburn or another chosen scheme with long-vowel/gemination rules
japanese.nlp: Lexicon/morphological analysis for Kanji; no learned model necessary for kana-only input
japanese.one_to_one: No for Kanji text; kana uses multi-character/context rules
japanese.implementation: Sudachi/MeCab-class reading pipeline plus deterministic kana renderer; user-provided readings for names
japanese.limits: Names and unusual readings can remain unresolved even with a large dictionary; accept reading overrides rather than claiming certainty.

korean.title: Korean: Hangul decomposition and standard-specific sound rules
korean.orthographic_method: Decompose Hangul syllables/Jamo consistently, then apply the selected spelling/romanization standard
korean.readable_method: Apply Revised Romanization-specific contextual rules and boundary/morphology handling; resolve Hanja with Korean lexical readings when present
korean.nlp: Rules first for Hangul; morphology/lexicon for exceptional boundaries, Hanja and conventional names
korean.one_to_one: No: syllable decomposition and cross-syllable rules
korean.implementation: Algorithmic Hangul core plus finite-state RR rules and optional lexical analysis
korean.limits: A general phonetic G2P output is not automatically Revised Romanization. A Hangul implementation does not cover all Hanja under composite script Kore.

thai.title: Thai: segmentation and lexical pronunciation
thai.orthographic_method: A reversible spelling scheme can be rule-based, but should not be labeled readable RTGS pronunciation
thai.readable_method: Word/syllable segmentation, lexical pronunciations and contextual reading followed by RTGS rendering; compare dictionary and compact neural engines
thai.nlp: Lexical/segmentation processing for reliable readable output; learned model optional
thai.one_to_one: No: vowel placement, syllable structure, silent letters and lexical readings
thai.implementation: PyThaiNLP-style tokenizer and pronunciation engine; evaluate thai2rom/ONNX against rule baselines
thai.limits: RTGS omits distinctions such as tone and is not a reversible source encoding. Names can use conventional spellings.

lao.title: Lao: syllable rules with lexical exception handling
lao.orthographic_method: Use a named spelling romanization with consonant/vowel-order and syllable rules
lao.readable_method: Language-specific syllable/word segmentation and pronunciation rules, with a lexicon for exceptions and ambiguous boundaries
lao.nlp: Rules plus segmentation/lexicon for reliable readable output; a neural model is not established as mandatory
lao.one_to_one: No: distributed vowel signs and syllable structure
lao.implementation: Finite-state syllable parser and Lao pronunciation lexicon; train a small model only for remaining errors
lao.limits: Do not apply Thai rules unchanged. Standard choice and tone preservation must be explicit.

khmer.title: Khmer: orthographic syllables, register and lexical readings
khmer.orthographic_method: Parse base/subscript consonants, vowel signs, series/register and modifiers using a named spelling scheme
khmer.readable_method: Combine syllable/register rules with word readings and exceptions; evaluate a specialist G2P model if lexical coverage is insufficient
khmer.nlp: Rules plus lexicon/segmentation for pronunciation-oriented output
khmer.one_to_one: No: consonant series changes vowel interpretation and words can have irregular readings
khmer.implementation: Khmer-specific orthographic parser plus lexical pronunciation layer
khmer.limits: A generic Brahmic/Indic transform is not a complete Khmer pronunciation engine.

myanmar.title: Myanmar/Burmese: structural spelling versus spoken readings
myanmar.orthographic_method: Normalize encoding under an explicit policy, parse orthographic syllables and render MLCTS or another named spelling scheme
myanmar.readable_method: Use Burmese lexical pronunciation and contextual syllable/tone rules; consider compact G2P for vocabulary generalization
myanmar.nlp: Lexicon/context for spoken-style romanization; rules for spelling conversion
myanmar.one_to_one: No: syllables, medials, combining signs and historical spellings
myanmar.implementation: Myanmar-specific parser, lexical readings and optional compact model
myanmar.limits: Zawgyi-to-Unicode detection/conversion is a separate preprocessing feature. Shared script does not permit reuse of Burmese phonology for Shan.

shan.title: Shan: language-specific syllable and tone rules
shan.orthographic_method: Map Shan-specific letters and tone/vowel marks with syllable-aware ordering under a chosen scheme
shan.readable_method: Apply Shan-specific readings and exceptions; evaluate lexical needs on native data before promising pronunciation coverage
shan.nlp: Rule-first baseline; lexical pronunciation requirements need language-specific validation
shan.one_to_one: No: syllabic context and combining signs
shan.implementation: Shan tables and finite-state syllable rules; no default Burmese reading model
shan.limits: A script-family inference supports implementation direction, not an accuracy claim for all Shan text.

tibetan.title: Tibetan Wylie spelling: stack parsing, with separate phonetic readings
tibetan.orthographic_method: Use the explicitly selected Tibetan Wylie scheme and parse stacked letters consistently; an extended Wylie scheme must be separately specified if offered
tibetan.readable_method: Select language/dialect, then use syllable/word lexicons and pronunciation rules or a specialist model
tibetan.nlp: No for structural spelling conversion; lexical/contextual processing for pronunciation
tibetan.one_to_one: No: stacks and historical spelling-to-speech differences
tibetan.implementation: Rule-based stack parser plus a separately selected Tibetan dialect/pronunciation layer
tibetan.limits: Wylie is not a phonetic spelling. Wylie and extended Wylie are distinct output contracts. Dzongkha has a separate profile despite sharing the script.

dzongkha.title: Dzongkha: Roman Dzongkha convention with lexical pronunciation work
dzongkha.orthographic_method: Parse the Tibetan-derived Dzongkha orthography with a declared spelling scheme; share only the low-level stack parser where appropriate
dzongkha.readable_method: Select the Dzongkha-specific Roman Dzongkha convention and supply Dzongkha lexical/phonological readings rather than Tibetan Wylie strings
dzongkha.nlp: Lexical/phonological processing for readable pronunciation; no general LLM is established as necessary
dzongkha.one_to_one: No: historical/stacked orthography does not directly spell every modern spoken form
dzongkha.implementation: Dzongkha-specific rules and reading data, with optional compact G2P if evaluation justifies it
dzongkha.limits: The named geographic romanization source has a bounded scope; native-reviewed ordinary-text and name coverage remains necessary. Do not treat a Tibetan pronunciation model as a Dzongkha model.

traditional-mongolian.title: Traditional Mongolian: structural spelling with separate lexical reading conversion
traditional-mongolian.orthographic_method: Map abstract letters under a chosen scheme; process variation selectors, joiners and suffix boundaries explicitly
traditional-mongolian.readable_method: Use Mongolian lexical/morphological information for modern pronunciation or Cyrillic correspondence; do not conflate glyph shaping and pronunciation
traditional-mongolian.nlp: No for source-spelling romanization; lexical/morphological processing for modern readable forms
traditional-mongolian.one_to_one: Not uniformly: control characters, variants and historical spelling
traditional-mongolian.implementation: Mongolian-specific structural rules plus optional lexical converter
traditional-mongolian.limits: This is distinct from straightforward Cyrillic Mongolian romanization.

syllabics.title: Inuktitut syllabics: deterministic syllable-to-Latin conversion
syllabics.orthographic_method: Map syllables and final consonants, vowel length and n/ng/nng sequences using the selected regional orthography
syllabics.readable_method: Use the corresponding standard Latin orthography; select dialect/region explicitly for orthographic differences
syllabics.nlp: No learned model for the script conversion baseline
syllabics.one_to_one: Syllable-to-string plus sequence rules, not letter-to-letter
syllabics.implementation: Tables and longest-match rules with explicit regional variants
syllabics.limits: Script conversion does not translate between Inuit language varieties or reconstruct a preferred personal-name spelling.

thaana.title: Dhivehi Thaana: consonant/vowel-mark algorithm
thaana.orthographic_method: Combine consonant letters with written vowel signs/sukun and apply the selected Dhivehi romanization scheme
thaana.readable_method: Language-specific contextual rules and conventional-name exceptions as needed
thaana.nlp: No learned model for standard spelling conversion
thaana.one_to_one: No: base letters plus combining vowel/absence-of-vowel marks
thaana.limits: Although written right-to-left, Thaana is not an Arabic-script transform.

meetei.title: Meetei Mayek: structural conversion with language-specific finals
meetei.orthographic_method: Map letters, dependent vowels, lonsum/final forms and punctuation under a selected scheme
meetei.readable_method: Apply Meitei syllable/reading conventions; add lexical exceptions only where required by evaluation
meetei.nlp: No learned model for structural romanization; pronunciation coverage requires native validation
meetei.one_to_one: No: dependent signs and final forms require rules
meetei.implementation: Meetei-specific parser/table; separate Bengali-script Meitei input mode
meetei.limits: Do not silently apply Bengali-language pronunciation to Bengali-script Meitei.

ol-chiki.title: Santali Ol Chiki: alphabetic mapping and modifier rules
ol-chiki.orthographic_method: Map Ol Chiki letters and phonetic modifiers under a chosen Santali Latin scheme
ol-chiki.readable_method: Preserve the selected Santali spelling conventions and significant marks
ol-chiki.nlp: No learned model for a standard script conversion baseline
ol-chiki.implementation: Small table and sequence rules; separate from Santali Latin identity profile
ol-chiki.limits: Do not handle Ol Chiki as a Devanagari-style inherent-vowel script.

nko.title: NKo: alphabetic conversion with combining tone/length marks
nko.orthographic_method: Normalize letters and combining marks, then apply a named NKo-to-Latin table preserving its tone/length policy
nko.readable_method: Use the chosen Manding language and Latin orthography where language-specific formatting differs
nko.nlp: No learned model for source-script conversion; explicit underlying-language policy may be needed
nko.one_to_one: Not strictly: marks and multicharacter outputs; reverse conversion can be ambiguous
nko.implementation: Table plus combining-mark and sequence rules
nko.limits: Google's bm-Nkoo label is a vendor catalog entry, not proof that NKo is a separate spoken language. The LOC table is not designed to be reversible.

tifinagh.title: Tifinagh Tamazight: standard-specific alphabet mapping
tifinagh.orthographic_method: Use a selected IRCAM/ALA-LC-compatible alphabet table and normalize punctuation/combining sequences
tifinagh.readable_method: Use the selected Tamazight variety's Latin orthography; conventional-name exceptions are optional
tifinagh.nlp: No learned model for alphabetic romanization
tifinagh.implementation: Small mapping table with a declared variety and standard
tifinagh.limits: A Tamazight macrolabel does not identify every Amazigh variety or its exact spelling conventions.

piqad.title: Klingon pIqaD: declared glyph/encoding conversion
piqad.orthographic_method: Require the precise vendor/private glyph encoding, then map to Klingon's Latin spelling
piqad.readable_method: Preserve the designed Klingon Latin orthography, including meaningful case and apostrophes
piqad.nlp: No language model for a declared glyph encoding conversion
piqad.one_to_one: Table-driven only after the encoding/font convention is known
piqad.implementation: Explicit encoding adapter and table; never guess arbitrary private-use glyph meanings
piqad.limits: The pIqaD mapping is not a universal Unicode character contract. Vendor translation support alone does not prove its public transliteration endpoint supports this conversion.
